1,200 repositories.

When we launched Patchwork CI, we made a promise: always free for open source. People told us we were crazy. "How will you make money?" they asked.

Losing our first big customer was the best thing that ever happened to Ledgerline.

Let me explain.

5 months in, they walked away, and it stung. A lot.

Failure isn't the opposite of success. It's part of it.

The reason they left? They had heavily customized their NetSuite instance, and we only supported standard fields. We weren't meeting them where they were.

So we did what great teams do: we listened, we learned, and we built. We spent 6 weeks adding support for custom fields. It wasn't just a feature. It changed how we think about our customers.

Today, we serve 38 customers, and 11 of them rely on custom fields.

The lesson is that your biggest setback can become your biggest breakthrough. Lean into the hard feedback. Your customers are telling you what to build, and you just have to listen.

What's a loss that shaped your company?

#Startups #SaaS #Leadership #CustomerSuccess #Growth

We built a beautiful app. Nobody used it.

When we launched Rotaship, we were proud of our sleek mobile app. We figured restaurant staff would love it.

That's when it hit us. We weren't solving the real problem. We were adding another one.

Restaurant teams don't want another app. They live on WhatsApp.

So in 2025 we made a tough call: we moved everything into WhatsApp.

The results: 140 outlets, and shift messages now get replies in under 20 minutes at the median.

Meet your users where they already are. Don't make them come to you.

Sometimes the best product decision is letting go of the thing you love.

#ProductManagement #Indonesia #StartupLessons #UserExperience

#Entrepreneurship #Africa #Shopify #AgencyLife #Pricing

After 11 years in a clinic, I walked away. Here's why.

I've always loved being a vet, but something kept breaking my heart. Day after day, I'd see anxious pets so terrified that we had to sedate them just to examine them. I knew there had to be a better way.

So in 2023, I took the leap and founded Doorstep Vet. The idea was simple: bring compassionate, high-quality care to pets in the one place they feel safest, their own home.

Two.

Hardware is hard. Here's our story.

Our very first production run at Shelfwise didn't go as planned. We shipped 400 labels with a faulty battery contact.

As a young hardware startup, it would have been easy to cut corners. But that's not who we are.

We made the call to recall and replace every single one of those 400 labels, at our own cost. It set us back about $7,000. Painful? Absolutely. Worth it? 100%.

Because trust is everything.

We didn't stop there. We introduced a 100% contact test at the factory. Since then, we've seen zero contact failures across 6,000 labels.

Mistakes don't define you. How you respond to them does.

To all the hardware founders out there: own your mistakes, fix them fast, and build systems so they never happen again.

#Hardware #Startups #Manufacturing #Leadership #Integrity
